key_insight: The Token-Energy Law estimates GPU-board joules per generated token using active weight bytes, private KV-history bytes, and realized decode time.
engineering_relevance: It helps engineers assess how batching, attended history length, and throughput affect decoding energy for a calibrated model and hardware/runtime configuration.
method: Separate logical byte demand into shared dense weights and per-request KV-history reads and updates.
Measure realized decode time as elapsed decoding duration divided by output tokens produced.
Combine both byte coordinates and time in an affine model with configuration-specific coefficients.
evidence_signal: Across three models using BF16 decoding on NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, including two-GPU tensor parallelism on Hopper, fixed-coefficient estimates using observed decode time differed from held-out condition-mean energy measurements by at most 3.73%.
watch_item: Validation is limited to dense, full-history decoding; new model or hardware/runtime configurations require calibration, and estimates rely on observed decode time.
paper_title: The Token-Energy Law of LLM Decode: Active Bytes and Realized Time Account for Joules per Token
